# yantra-core

> The orchestration logic for Yantra, with no opinion about who calls it. Reaches machines over the
> system `ssh` binary, opens tmux sessions on them, launches and observes Claude Code, and reads the
> Tailscale inventory. A library: it never prints and never exits (ADR-0005). The CLI calls it
> in-process today; `yantrad` will call the same functions from an HTTP handler.

Every module below has a `//!` header explaining *why* it is shaped the way it is, usually naming the
invariant that forced it. Those headers are the real documentation — the notes here say which file to
open, not what it contains.

## Entry points

Each takes a workspace name — `doctor` a machine name — loads it from
`~/.config/yantra/workspaces/<name>.toml`, and opens an ssh connection. Each also exposes a generic
half taking an `Exec`, which is what the tests drive.

- [up.rs](src/up.rs): open a workspace's tmux session, optionally launching an agent in it. Idempotent — a second call attaches. Returns `Opened::{Created,Attached}`. **On macOS it refuses when no tmux server is running rather than starting one** ([ADR-0018](../../docs/adr/0018-the-tmux-server-carries-the-macos-login-session.md) §1, Y-151): a server started over ssh forks panes that cannot read the login keychain (I-44). The far side's OS arrives as an argument of the generic half, so a container test on Linux drives that branch.
- [resume.rs](src/resume.rs): put the agent back on the conversation it left off, via `claude --continue --fork-session`. Refuses rather than guesses when the pane holds something it did not start. Carries ADR-0018 §1 too, and asks it before the gate rather than leaving it to `up::open` — every plan but one prepares the agent first.
- [logs.rs](src/logs.rs): read the agent's transcript JSONL, projected down to turns. Selection happens on the far side.
- [tokens.rs](src/tokens.rs): add up what a session spent — input, output, cache-write and cache-read — from the same transcript, found by the same script, **grouped by the model that spent it** because models do not share a rate. Every figure is one Claude Code recorded; the file holds no cost field. **Counts API responses, not records** (I-61): one response is written once per content block with the same `requestId` and the same usage, and summing per record reported 13,968,868 cache-read tokens against a true 7,492,711. Three fields are read for [price.rs](src/price.rs) rather than for the counts — `model`, `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` and `speed` — and I-62 is what each of them is guarding. What crosses the wire is numbers, so the conversation stays where it was written. **`since` counts only the responses stamped at or after it** (Y-354): the last `timestamp` on a record places it, a response is marked seen before the window is checked so one that straddles the start counts zero times (I-61), and a record with no stamp is dropped under a window.
- [price.rs](src/price.rs): dollars per million tokens, written down rather than fetched — Anthropic publishes no price API, and reaching the public internet to answer *what did this cost* would spend the property this project is built on. Two numbers per model: the cache prices are multipliers of base input (1.25× for a five-minute write, 2× for an hour, 0.1× for a read), which is how the published table is built. **A written-down table reports wrong money the day a price changes**, so `AS_OF` is printed beside every figure derived from it — the owner's choice over the alternative of saying nothing. A model it does not carry has no rate rather than a zero one.
- [status.rs](src/status.rs): is the agent running, finished, stopped, crashed or killed. Reads two sources and reports their disagreement rather than resolving it.
- [remove.rs](src/remove.rs): deleting a workspace, and the session it would leave behind. [edit.rs](src/edit.rs)'s refusal with the field removed rather than moved — same guard, different wording, because a move can be undone and a delete cannot. `force` skips asking the machine rather than ignoring its answer. The file half is `workspace::remove`, which deletes a file that will not parse and loses only the description.
- [probe.rs](src/probe.rs): ask a machine whether a directory is there and what git `origin` it holds, before a workspace names it. `up` asks the same question at [up.rs](src/up.rs) but only *after* the file exists, so a mistyped path is found by the verb meant to start working. One round trip: the origin question only makes sense when the first answers yes, and a person is waiting on both. `git`'s failure is swallowed deliberately — *not a repository* and *no origin* are both "no origin here". Reached over a `POST` ([ADR-0019](../../docs/adr/0019-a-probe-that-asks-a-machine-is-a-post.md)), because no snapshot can hold an answer about a path nobody has typed.
- [clone.rs](src/clone.rs): clone a repository onto a machine inside a tmux session there (Y-344). `plan` checks both values before any machine is asked (I-24): the URL is `https://`, `ssh://` or `user@host:path` and carries no credential, because a credential in the URL would sit in the pane's start command for as long as the session lives ([ADR-0023 §4](../../docs/adr/0023-the-github-grant-lives-beside-the-relay.md)); the destination is absolute or `~/…`, never climbs and holds only `-_./+@`. Then `git clone --progress` is the startup command of a session named `clone-<slug>`, opened with `Tmux::ensure`, so a second ask attaches (I-30) and nothing waits for the clone — the pane under `remain-on-exit` is the progress and the ending (I-4), and [probe.rs](src/probe.rs) is the answer. `~/` is completed by the far side's own `$HOME`, because `sq` would make the `~` a literal. On macOS with no tmux server it refuses as `up` does (ADR-0018 §1). [tests/clone.rs](tests/clone.rs) clones a bare repository inside the container over the container's own sshd, with a key the container's user holds.
- [install.rs](src/install.rs): install what a machine is missing of `tmux`, `git` and `claude`, and nothing else ([ADR-0028](../../docs/adr/0028-yantra-installs-the-bare-minimum-on-a-machine.md), Y-386) — plus the microphone when the caller asks ([ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-the-microphone-reaches-a-machine-as-a-virtual-source.md) §1–3, Y-417). The `Mic` step is not in `BASICS` and is reported only when asked for: its PipeWire packages join the same package run under the same `sudo -n` rule, then linger (`sudo -n loginctl enable-linger`, or the command left for the one-off terminal), the per-user drop-in written whole, `pipewire-pulse` restarted until `yantra-mic` appears, and `pactl set-default-source yantra-mic` only where the card list (`/proc/asound/cards`, a parameter of `of`) shows no card. The sink is `media.class=Audio/Sink/Virtual`, which keeps it out of WirePlumber's default-sink choice. A second run is `Present` and restarts nothing. `check_machine` refuses a name that is not a hostname before anything reaches ssh: dot-separated labels of letters, digits and `-`, none starting with `-`, at most 253 characters. Each tool is looked for with the predicate `doctor` reports on. `tmux` and `git` come from the machine's own package manager (`apt-get`, `dnf`, `pacman`, `apk`, `zypper`, `brew`), and root is `sudo -n` and nothing more: a sudo that wants a password returns `ForYou { SudoAsks }` with the exact command for a person, a sudo that refuses the account or no sudo at all names the command for root, and macOS with no Homebrew names Homebrew's installer or the Command Line Tools. `claude` comes from the vendor's installer, after its prerequisites come through the same package run — `curl` and `bash`, and on musl `libgcc`, `libstdc++` and `ripgrep`; no file is written, and [agent.rs](src/agent.rs) sets `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` at launch on musl ([ADR-0028](../../docs/adr/0028-yantra-installs-the-bare-minimum-on-a-machine.md) §5's note) — so where that run stops, the `claude` step stops with it. A `claude` that is found and whose `--version` fails is `Failed`. Installer output loses its terminal escape sequences. Each tool is asked for again afterwards, so an installer that exits 0 and leaves nothing Yantra can find is `Failed` with the end of its output. [tests/install.rs](tests/install.rs) runs the real `apk` and sudo in the container, with a local stand-in for the vendor's installer.
- [about.rs](src/about.rs): the three build facts — version, target triple, build date — from one `build.rs` here rather than one per binary (Y-343): every binary compiles this crate for its own target in the same build and the workspace has one version. `newer` says whether a published `Release` is newer than this build, by number and not by text (Y-367), so About and `yantra update --check` cannot disagree.
- [dirs.rs](src/dirs.rs): ask a machine what one directory holds, so a form can walk to a path rather than trust one that was typed. **`make` beside it** (Y-344) makes one directory under the path with `mkdir -p` — a directory already there is the state asked for — under a parent that must already exist, and lists the path again; the name is one segment with no leading dot, refused otherwise (I-24). One level with the git repositories marked and their `origin` beside them, in one round trip for [probe.rs](src/probe.rs)'s reason — and **never a sweep**: [D4](../../docs/archive/design/04-workspace-creation.md) §2 measured `find $HOME -maxdepth 4 -name .git` at 8.5 s over ssh to this fleet's Mac against 0.026 s on its Linux box, while one level costs what a probe costs. It recurses nothing and caches nothing. **Since Y-414 it lists everything at that level** (owner, 2026-09-29, reversing D4 §3.1): files, dotfiles and directories the login account cannot enter, each marked (`Kind`, `access`), directories first. It classifies with `test` builtins only, so GNU and BSD far sides answer alike, and a symlink to a directory is a directory. It stops at `CAP` (2000) entries and says so (`truncated`), and a directory the account cannot read is a listing with `access: false`, not an error. Records come back **NUL-separated**, so a name holding a newline arrives whole or not at all — a path is the one string a filesystem lets hold anything but `/` and NUL. **An empty directory and a path that is not there are different answers**: the first is a listing, the second an error naming the machine and the path (R-23).
- [down.rs](src/down.rs): stop the session, reporting how the agent ended — read *before* the pane that holds the exit status is destroyed.
- [sessions.rs](src/sessions.rs): every tmux session on every machine a workspace names **or the tailnet offers** (Y-176), queried concurrently, partial answers reported rather than failed. Tailnet membership is a *candidate*, never a resolution — `~/.ssh/config` still decides what a name means (ADR-0009), and a candidate that is not an ssh destination comes back as that machine's `Err`. `worth_asking` skips phones and offline peers because `refresh.rs` polls this every 30 s and an unreachable candidate costs a full `ConnectTimeout` each time. `kill` stops one by machine and name (Y-178) — **not** `down`, which reads how the agent ended first; a session Yantra did not start has no ending to read. It asks whether the session is there before killing, because `Tmux::kill` treats absence as success and so cannot say which happened.
- [attention.rs](src/attention.rs): what GitHub is waiting on you for — `Item`, `Attention`, and the `Forge` trait the layers above are faked against. The wire moved to [github.rs](src/github.rs) in Y-342; before that this spawned `gh` and held no credential, which the appliance cannot do (Q20, [ADR-0023](../../docs/adr/0023-the-github-grant-lives-beside-the-relay.md)).
- [github.rs](src/github.rs): GitHub read and written with the grant this process holds (Y-342, [ADR-0023](../../docs/adr/0023-the-github-grant-lives-beside-the-relay.md)). The device flow — `begin`, `poll`, and `wait`, which adds five seconds on `slow_down` and keeps them, and names `expired_token`, `access_denied` and the rest as typed errors; `login_name` from `GET /user`; `repos` over `GET /user/repos` following `Link` page by page; and `attention` as two REST searches and a notification count read off `Link` with one item per page. `latest_release` (Y-367, [ADR-0027](../../docs/adr/0027-the-appliance-pulls-its-own-update.md) §4) reads `tag_name` from `GET /repos/2002Bishwajeet/yantra/releases/latest`, with a `Bearer` only when it holds a grant; a tag that is not `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` is `NotAVersion`, and a rate-limited `403` stays `Status`. For the coding loop (Y-488, [ADR-0034](../../docs/adr/0034-the-coding-loop-writes-to-github.md)): `IssueRef` parses and prints `owner/repo#n` and refuses anything else as `NotAnIssue`; `issue` reads a title and body from `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}` and refuses a PR as `IsAPull`; `pull_for_head` reads the newest PR from `owner:branch` in any state, `merged_at` making it merged; `default_branch` reads `GET /repos/{o}/{r}`, and `create_pull` posts `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls` as JSON (Y-449), a 422 being `Unprocessable` with GitHub's two messages, read from an `errors[]` entry that is an object or a plain string, and never the title or body; `repo_of` reads `(owner, repo)` off a github.com remote in its https, `ssh://` and scp forms. `Issue` does not print its text, and no error carries it. `Token` and `Device` print none of what they hold, no error carries either, and every send runs on a blocking thread (I-13). `TOKEN` is `YANTRA_GITHUB_TOKEN`, read from the environment by `from_env`; `client_id` is `YANTRA_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` from the environment or a build-time default, and every flow refuses without one. `Github::at` puts a loopback listener where GitHub would be, which is how the wire is tested; `tests/github_api.rs` is the ignored test against the real one.
- [doctor.rs](src/doctor.rs): whether a machine can do what Yantra will ask of it — the eleven checks in [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md), each **present, absent or unknown**. A **read**: it installs nothing and starts nothing, including the tmux server the macOS branch asks about (ADR-0018 §1). Every branch answers `unknown` where it could not ask, which is R-23 and the whole shape of the module: *absent* sends a reader to install something and *unknown* sends them to the machine. Two answers are narrower than they look — `heartbeat` is unknown from anything that is not the daemon holding the beats (ADR-0012, Y-044), which `yantrad` fills in for itself on `GET /api/readiness` (Y-168) rather than this module ever answering it, and `provider-auth` discards its output on the far side, because a real `gh auth status` names the account (§B4). `mic` (ADR-0031 §9) is *absent* with *not installed* where the microphone was never set up, and names linger whenever the drop-in is there and linger is off, a listed source included, since that source stops at the next logout. `github` is a twelfth check that is in none of the eleven: a pure mapper over `GET /user`'s answer about the grant **this** host holds rather than about a machine being swept, so no grant and a refused grant are the two *absent*s and everything else — an unreachable GitHub included — is *unknown* (Y-175, Y-342). When `reachable` fails for a machine no `Host` block in the ssh config names, `machine` says so first and points at the join command (Y-412, [identity.rs](src/identity.rs) `unnamed_in`).
- [edit.rs](src/edit.rs): change a workspace after it exists. `repo` and `startup` are inert until the next `up`; `machine` is where the session lives, so moving it while a session is open there is **refused** rather than performed — and a machine that cannot be asked is refused too, never assumed empty (R-23).

## Primitives

- [ssh.rs](src/ssh.rs): one command on one machine, over the system `ssh` with `ControlMaster`. Sentinel trailer, base64 payload, `-E` to divert ssh's own diagnostics. ADR-0006. `exec` runs at `LogLevel=INFO` and the payload marks where the command's stderr starts, so a server's banner — Tailscale SSH's refusal — reaches a transport error and never a command's stderr (Y-412). Every connection also gets **Yantra's own `known_hosts`** beside the control sockets, with `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`, so first contact needs nobody to type anything and a *changed* host key is a hard refusal — measured in [tests/ssh_identity.rs](tests/ssh_identity.rs) rather than assumed. Also `os()` — `uname -s` over that envelope, because ADR-0009 leaves no key joining a workspace's `machine` to a Tailscale `MachineInfo` and ADR-0013's heartbeat may not carry one. A `uname` that did not answer is an error, never a default (R-23). **`stdio` is the fourth call shape** (Y-433): a long-lived command whose stdin and stdout are the conversation, with no sentinel, the command still base64 but `exec`ed rather than piped into `/bin/sh`, so its stdin stays ssh's. The expansion sits in single quotes for `/bin/sh` alone, so a csh or fish login shell never parses it, and it runs at `LogLevel=INFO` as `exec` does, so a Tailscale refusal still reaches the error (Y-443). Its `ssh` runs in a process group of its own (Y-419): a terminal's Ctrl-C would otherwise end it before the far side drains.
- [acp.rs](src/acp.rs): an ACP v1 client for Codex, Gemini, Grok and opencode ([ADR-0033](../../docs/adr/0033-other-harnesses-speak-acp-and-claude-delegates.md), Y-433). `Agent::start` runs the harness's command (R19 §1) over `Ssh::stdio`; `Agent::over` is the generic half on any pair of streams. JSON-RPC by hand: `initialize` (refuses any version but 1), `new_session`, `load_session`, `prompt`, `cancel` and `answer` for a permission request. **No ACP shape leaves this file**, because v2 changes `session/load`, the prompt result and the diff. Updates come out as [chat.rs](src/chat.rs) events on a channel; a request for `fs` or `terminal` gets -32601, and a closed agent's error carries the end of its stderr so "not found" can be read. `Harness` parses from and prints its name, `Error::is_auth` reads R19's login refusals, `login_command` names the command for each harness, and `Capabilities::login` is the agent's own auth-method description. `Agent::kept` runs an agent a keeper holds, with a cursor on each event, and `Agent::resume` continues one an earlier daemon started, from `replay` of its journals; this daemon's JSON-RPC ids carry a random prefix, so they never meet an earlier daemon's in `in` (ADR-0035 decision 9). [tests/acp.rs](tests/acp.rs) runs it against a real `opencode acp` in the fixture.
- [mic.rs](src/mic.rs): the writer behind the dashboard's push-to-talk ([ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-the-microphone-reaches-a-machine-as-a-virtual-source.md) §5, Y-418). `open` runs `WRITER`, the ADR's `pw-cat --playback --raw --target yantra-mic-sink` line, over `Ssh::stdio`; `open_at` names the machine the way `~/.ssh/config` does. A `Stream` takes 16 kHz mono s16le with `write`, and `close` shuts stdin, which ends `pw-cat`, and waits five seconds for it. A non-zero exit carries the end of stderr and ssh's log. `stopped` resolves when the writer exits on its own. `Stream::over` is the same on any writer, for tests. No buffer, no log of a payload, and dropping it kills the local `ssh`. The real-machine proof is [yantrad's tests/mic.rs](../yantrad/tests/mic.rs). **`yantra mic` adds the laptop half** (§7, Y-419): `RECORDER` is `pw-record --raw --format s16 --rate 16000 --channels 1 -`, `record` starts it here and maps a missing binary to `NoRecorder`, and `relay` copies about 640 bytes at a time into a `Stream` until the recorder ends (`Ended::Recorder`), the caller's `stop` resolves (`Ended::Stopped`) or the writer exits (`Error::Ended`). A failed read is `Error::Record`. Its proof is [yantra's tests/mic.rs](../yantra/tests/mic.rs).
- [image.rs](src/image.rs): an image pasted into the chat (Y-424). `kind` reads PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP from the magic bytes and never trusts a browser's type. `Images::of` is a thread's directory, `images/` under its keeper's `~/.yantra/keep/<workspace>/<thread>` (Y-447), outside every repository and worktree. `put` sends the bytes on `Ssh::stdio`'s stdin (I-20, I-26) to `umask 077; mkdir -p "$d" && cat > "$d/<n>.<ext>"`, where `<n>` is a counter (I-24), and returns the absolute path the machine printed; `put_with` is the generic half. `remove` deletes the directory through `Exec`, and `thread::remove` deletes it with the thread. Errors: `NotAnImage`, `Ssh`, `Put` with the stderr tail and ssh's log, and `Remove`. No byte or size is logged. [tests/image.rs](tests/image.rs) proves a 10 MB image lands whole in a 0700 directory and goes with `remove`.
- [keep.rs](src/keep.rs) and [keep.sh](src/keep.sh): the keeper that holds a chat turn on its machine (Y-447, [ADR-0035](../../docs/adr/0035-a-chat-turn-outlives-its-ssh-pipe.md)). The tmux session `yantra-keep-<workspace>-<thread>` runs `keep.sh`, which feeds the agent from the journal `in` and writes its stdout to `out` and its stderr to `err`, in `~/.yantra/keep/<workspace>/<thread>/`, mode 0700. `start` runs a plain `new-session` (`Busy` on `duplicate session`, I-1), sets `remain-on-exit` (I-4) and `respawn-pane -k`s the script in the base64 envelope (I-29, I-26, I-35) on the pane's `%id` (I-21); it resets the journals and keeps `images/`, and writes `run` and `mode`. `append` writes a line to `in` at a known offset, so a retry never doubles it; `feed` is the writer over it, and `close_stdin` ends the agent's input. All three carry the keeper's `run` and do nothing to a keeper of another run (Y-542). `follow` is a reconnecting reader of `out` from an offset, a far `tail` that stops when the pane is dead. The reader and the writer end when their owner drops them, or after a machine silent for the keeper's idle limit. `read` reads a journal whole, `size` measures one, `pane` finds the keeper's pane, or none once the session is gone, and `kill` removes the session (I-30). `Limits` are the output cap and the idle time `keep.sh` enforces (ADR-0035 decision 5). `Cursor` is `<run>:<line end>:<part>` and orders events in one run. `PREFIX` and `is_keeper` are what `workspace::validate_name` refuses and `sessions` hides. [tests/keep.rs](tests/keep.rs) runs a real keeper in the fixture.
- [delegate.rs](src/delegate.rs): a delegated task ([ADR-0033](../../docs/adr/0033-other-harnesses-speak-acp-and-claude-delegates.md) decisions 4 and 5, Y-435). `Task::start` makes a worktree of the repository at `~/.yantra/worktrees/<id>` on a new branch `yantra/<id>`, starts an ACP agent in it and sends one prompt. The task answers each permission request with the agent's own "allow once", because the worktree is the isolation. `progress` reads memory only: the state, the agent's last message and the diff summary, which the task takes when its turn ends. `steer` cancels a running turn and sends its prompt as the next turn of the same session, as T3 Code steers an ACP agent (Y-454); a steer before the first turn begins waits for it, two steers join with a blank line, and an ended or stopping task refuses one with `Error::Ended`. `wait` waits on memory for the task to settle: it ends and takes its last summary. `stop` cancels the turn, ends the agent and takes the summary, and leaves the worktree for review; `remove` deletes the worktree and the branch, and succeeds when either is already gone. A task whose agent never opened a session removes its own worktree. A `repo` that is not `/…` or `~/…` is refused before ssh. [tests/delegate.rs](tests/delegate.rs) runs it against real git and a real `opencode acp`.
- [thread.rs](src/thread.rs): a chat session's own git worktree (Y-359, the isolate answer in [ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-the-chat-is-a-stream-json-bridge-in-the-daemon.md)'s 2026-10-06 amendment). `open` makes `~/.yantra/worktrees/chat/<workspace>/<id>` on the branch `yantra/chat/<workspace>/<id>` with [delegate.rs](src/delegate.rs)'s worktree code, and a live session in the repository does not stop it. `list` reads `git worktree list --porcelain -z`, so a thread survives a daemon restart. `remember` and `recall` keep an ACP thread's harness and session id in git config as `branch.<branch>.yantraHarness` and `yantraSession` (Y-434); a thread with neither is Claude's, and `branch -D` forgets both. `open_for_issue` keeps `branch.<branch>.yantraIssue = owner/repo#n` and removes the thread if it cannot (Y-488); `listed` adds each thread's issue and upstream (git's own `branch.<b>.remote`/`merge` and the remote's URL) in one more round trip. `threads` and `start` are the entry points `yantra chat ls`/`chat new` and the daemon share: `threads` derives each `Pr` from the upstream through `pulls?head=`, and is `Unknown` with no grant; `start` reads the issue before it opens a worktree and returns `draft`. `logs`, `spent` and `status` read the worktree's path, because Claude Code files the transcript under the directory it ran in. Ending a session deletes nothing; `remove` deletes the worktree and the branch, and is the only path that does. [tests/thread.rs](tests/thread.rs) proves it against real git, a real sshd and a live tmux pane.
- [checkpoint.rs](src/checkpoint.rs): checkpoints of a chat thread's worktree, and a revert to one (Y-448). The shape is T3 Code's `CheckpointStore.ts` and the checkpoint operations of `GitVcsDriver.ts` at `72d5c32`, credited in its block comment ([ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-the-chat-is-a-stream-json-bridge-in-the-daemon.md) decision 5). A checkpoint is a parentless commit of the whole tree, made through a private `GIT_INDEX_FILE` with `add -A`, `write-tree` and `commit-tree`, under `refs/yantra/checkpoints/<thread id>/<n>`; no branch moves. `base` keeps checkpoint 0 when the thread has none, `capture` keeps the next one and returns its number, `diff` is checkpoint `n - 1` to `n`, cut at 256 KiB on a character boundary, and `revert` restores the files and leaves the index at `HEAD`, then deletes every checkpoint above it. `branch` (Y-490, Y-543) is the thread's worktree, untracked files too, against `merge-base HEAD <start> <repository HEAD>`, so a main checkout on an older branch does not move the base: a `BranchDiff` with the base, the `FileStat`s (a rename's old path, no counts for a binary file) cut at a whole record, and the unified diff cut as `diff` cuts it. One `diff --numstat -p -z -M` pass against the worktree reads both, through a private index where `add -A -N` marks untracked files, so no blob is written. Only a merge-base that finds no commit adds a line of Yantra's to git's words. Errors: `NoCheckpoint`, `Git` with git's words, and `Ssh`. `thread::remove` deletes the refs. [tests/checkpoint.rs](tests/checkpoint.rs) proves a revert and a branch diff against real git in the fixture, which has no git identity.
- [commit.rs](src/commit.rs): commit and push a chat thread's branch (Y-492, [ADR-0034](../../docs/adr/0034-the-coding-loop-writes-to-github.md) decisions 2 and 5). One remote command per call in the thread's worktree; every path, ref and message goes through `sq`. `draft` snapshots the tree through a private index, untracked files too, and pipes T3 Code's prompt, a `--stat` and the patch (capped at 256 KiB) into `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema` with no tools, slash commands, MCP servers, hooks or session, run from a fresh `mktemp -d` so no transcript lands under the worktree; it reads `structured_output`, then `result`. `commit` asks `git var` for both identities with `user.useConfigOnly`, then `add -A` and `commit`, with hooks; it never uses the checkpoint identity. `push` reads `branch.<b>.remote` and `.merge`, or pushes to `origin` as `yantra/<n>-<id>` (`yantra/<id>` without an issue), always with an explicit refspec and `-u`, never forced; it returns the remote's name, never its URL, and drops a credential from git's errors. Errors: `Claude`, `NoIdentity`, `NothingToCommit`, `NoRemote`, `Refused` (a porcelain `!` line), `Git` and `Ssh`; `draft_for`, `commit_for` and `push_for` add `Failed` with `Workspace`, `NoThread`, `Thread` and `NoStateDir`. `open_pr` (Y-449, decisions 1 and 3) refuses a thread with no upstream (`NotPushed`) and an upstream not on github.com (`NotGithub`), then answers a PR already open with `created: false` before it reads the tip. The tip read refuses a branch that is `Ahead` of, `Behind` or `Diverged` from its remote-tracking tip. It posts to the default branch with the tip commit's subject and body (`NoTitle` when both are blank) and `Closes #n` for an issue thread unless the body already closes it; a 422 "already exists" re-reads the winner and answers it with `created: false`. GitHub's 404 is `Unseen`, and its other failures are `Github`. `open_pr_for` is its wrapper. The prompt and flags are T3 Code's `ClaudeTextGeneration.ts` at `1451e7c`, credited in its block comment. [tests/commit.rs](tests/commit.rs) proves no identity, a commit, nothing to commit, a push and two refused pushes against real git in the fixture, with a stubbed `claude`, and `open_pr`'s tip read over the real ssh exec against a loopback GitHub.
- [chat.rs](src/chat.rs): the provider-neutral chat event model ([ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-the-chat-is-a-stream-json-bridge-in-the-daemon.md) decision 1) — content deltas, tool items, permission requests, plans, token usage, turn and thread lifecycle — in T3 Code's vocabulary, credited in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Serialised as `{threadId, type, payload}` so a relay sends it unchanged. It holds only what its sources produce: ACP v1, Claude's stream-json and [checkpoint.rs](src/checkpoint.rs). `thread.started` names the thread and its harness, a failed `turn.completed` carries a `message`, `request.opened` has a `title`, `turn.diff.updated` carries a turn's unified diff, and `thread.reverted` names the checkpoint the files went back to. `PermissionMode` holds T3 Code's four modes (Y-453), Supervised by default, and `answers` says which request a mode accepts without asking.
- [claude.rs](src/claude.rs): a chat turn with Claude Code (ADR-0026 decision 2, Y-356, [R20](../../docs/research/20-claude-stream-json-turn.md)). `Turn::start` runs `cd <worktree> && exec claude [--add-dir <images>] [--mcp-config <room server> --allowedTools <room tools>] [--permission-mode auto|acceptEdits] -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio [--resume <newest transcript>]` over `Ssh::stdio` and writes one `user` line; `--add-dir` names the chat's [image.rs](src/image.rs) directory, so Claude reads a pasted image without a prompt (Y-424); `command`'s `Mcp` adds `yantrad`'s `/api/mcp` as the HTTP server `yantra-room`, with `X-Yantra-Thread: <workspace>/<thread>`, and allows its two tools so a woken turn needs no prompt for them (Y-534); the Auto and Auto-accept edits modes add Claude's own `--permission-mode` (Y-453), and `answers` leaves the daemon nothing to accept in them; `Turn::over` is the generic half. stdout maps to [chat.rs](src/chat.rs) events: `init` starts the turn, deltas stream, a `tool_use` starts an item and its `tool_result` completes it, `can_use_tool` opens a request, and `result` sends the usage, completes the turn and closes stdin. `answer` writes the `control_response` (Accept, Accept always with Claude's suggestions for this session only, Decline); `cancel` sends `interrupt` and closes stdin. An exit with no `result` fails the turn with the stderr tail. `Turn::kept` reads a turn a keeper holds, with a cursor on each event, and `Turn::resume` continues one from `replay` of its journals without sending the replayed events again (Y-447). **No stream-json shape leaves this file.** Unit tests replay scrubbed 2.1.291 recordings in [tests/recordings/](tests/recordings/); [tests/claude.rs](tests/claude.rs) runs a real `claude` in the fixture with the owner's login, and shows it reads a pasted red PNG.
- [room.rs](src/room.rs): the rooms live agents talk in ([ADR-0038](../../docs/adr/0038-rooms-and-guest-devices.md) decisions 1 to 5, Y-534). Pure logic with an injected clock; `yantrad` holds a `Rooms` in memory. A name is `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`. A room keeps the last 200 messages or 1 MiB, refuses a message over 16 KiB, and counts `seq` from 1. Either tool makes or joins a room. A member is a node plus an optional `workspace/thread`, or with no thread an MCP session id, so two sessions on one node are two members. It starts its cursor at the room's last message, and expires 24 h after its last call; a room with no member and no message then goes. `send` answers `seq`, `delivered` (the other live members) and the member threads to wake, never the sender. `read` leaves out the reader's own messages and moves its cursor; `deliver` does the same for a wake without keeping the member alive, and `give_back` returns a failed wake's messages to the member's next read or wake. `session_id` is 128 random bits in hex. The 20th agent message pauses the room and wakes nothing, later sends are refused, and `resume` sets the count to 0. `wrap` makes `<room name from seq budget>` and escapes every `<room` and `</room` in the text, in any case, and every quote in an attribute. `cap` keeps a woken turn at `acceptEdits` at most. `tools`, `call` and `PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` are what both MCP transports serve.
- [tmux.rs](src/tmux.rs): resolve the binary absolutely, create sessions idempotently, list them, read a pane's ending, kill, and wrap a command so the **server** forks it (`run_shell`, ADR-0018 §5). The densest invariant surface in the crate.
- [agent.rs](src/agent.rs): find `claude`, check the credential, build the launch command, read the running-agent registry. The launch command exports `PIPEWIRE_NODE=yantra-mic` on every start, so ALSA's `default` records from the virtual microphone for the agent alone (ADR-0031 §3). **On macOS the check runs through `tmux run-shell` in the server that will fork the agent** (ADR-0018 §5, Y-151), because the answer depends on which process asks — over ssh it is a `Background` process and answers `loggedIn: false` there forever (I-44). What a pass claims stays bounded by **I-53**: a credential was found, never that it works. Claude Code only, per the one-agent-first guardrail. Its `CANDIDATES` is public because `yantra-agent`'s label probe searches the same directories for the same reason (I-34), and so is `locate` — the probe itself, which [doctor.rs](src/doctor.rs) points at `gh` and `glab`. It takes a `&'static str`, because the name is interpolated into a remote shell command.
- [identity.rs](src/identity.rs): the ssh identity this account reaches the fleet with (Y-144) — an ed25519 key with **no passphrase**, because `BatchMode=yes` has nowhere to type one and an agent is a login session an appliance does not have, and one `Host` block per machine a workspace names binding that key with `IdentitiesOnly`. Idempotent in both halves: an existing key is kept, because regenerating orphans every `authorized_keys` entry, and a machine the config already names is left exactly as it is — that block is ADR-0009's escape hatch and Yantra is not the authority on what a name means. It writes **no `known_hosts`**: [ssh.rs](src/ssh.rs) already gives every connection its own with `accept-new`. `HostName`, `Port`, `User` and `ProxyJump` are the owner's half of [D2 §2](../../docs/design/02-setup.md)'s boundary, and so is placing the public key. A `machine` that is not one `Host` pattern is **refused before anything is written**: nothing validates that field as an ssh destination (ADR-0009), so a name carrying a newline would write config lines of its own into the file that decides how every connection is made. **`describe` is the read half** (Y-343): the public key, its kind and the fingerprint `ssh-keygen -l` prints, `None` when there is no key yet, and it generates nothing — which is what lets `GET /api/ssh-identity` sit on a route a browser opens. The private half is never read. **`join_in` is one machine's block with `User`** (Y-387, [ADR-0029](../../docs/adr/0029-a-machine-joins-itself.md)): the account the join command ran as, checked as one plain token before anything is written, and never written over a config that already names the machine. `host_of` is the host `ssh -G` resolves a destination to, which `yantrad` matches against a Tailscale node to route a room call (Y-534).
- [join.rs](src/join.rs) and [join.sh](src/join.sh): the join command (Y-387, ADR-0029). A POSIX `sh` script with the daemon's address, its public key and its version filled in; it asks before each root step, reading `/dev/tty` because `curl | sh` makes stdin the script, and `YANTRA_JOIN_ANSWER` answers every question for a test. A key holding a quote or a newline is refused. Its podman test is [yantrad's tests/join.rs](../yantrad/tests/join.rs).
- [terminfo.rs](src/terminfo.rs): pass the caller's `TERM` through when the far side knows it, fall back when it does not, install on request.
- [inventory.rs](src/inventory.rs): `tailscale status --json` behind a trait, plus `whois`/`owner` for ADR-0016's live authorisation. Read-only and advisory — it observes machines, it never resolves them (ADR-0009). **I-52**: `whois` and `status` name the same node's identity under different keys (`StableID` vs `ID`, `User` vs `UserID`) and the mismatch parses silently, so they need separate structs.
- [update.rs](src/update.rs): asking the appliance to install the current release ([ADR-0027](../../docs/adr/0027-the-appliance-pulls-its-own-update.md) §3, Y-368). `request` is the daemon's half: it creates the empty `TRIGGER` that `yantra-update.path` watches, and refuses with `NotInstalled` when `UPDATER` is absent — the paths are parameters so a test names a scratch directory. `apply` is the CLI's half: `systemctl start --no-ask-password yantra-update.service`, read by exit code and then by words, since polkit's refusal and a failed unit both exit 1. Neither passes a version.
- [workspace.rs](src/workspace.rs): the TOML schema. `deny_unknown_fields`, because a silently ignored key is the worst kind of bug (ADR-0007). `create` writes one (Y-116's CLI half) and **refuses to overwrite**; it validates neither `machine` nor `repo`, because ADR-0009 has Yantra never resolving a machine and `repo` is a path on the far side that `up` already checks there (Y-081). It does refuse an **empty** `machine`, `repo` or `startup` (Y-119) — an absent `startup` is what means *just a shell*, so a blank one is a command that cannot run rather than a second spelling of absence. **`load` refuses the same three, by asking the same predicate** (Y-137), naming the file, the field and the workspace. **`list` returns a `Listing`** (Y-141): the workspaces that loaded, and every file that did not under its name with its reason, so one broken file costs only itself — the outer `Result` is what is left of the old all-or-nothing rule and is about the directory rather than a file in it. `update` is the counterpart Y-126 added: it rewrites only the fields named, renames the new file over the old one, and knows nothing about sessions — that refusal is [edit.rs](src/edit.rs)'s. **`repair` is the one write that composes nothing** ([ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-a-raw-write-only-from-broken-to-valid.md), Y-190): it takes a whole file's bytes, and two refusals bound it — a file that parses is `Loads`, and bytes that do not are the `parse` error itself, naming what is still wrong. So it can move a file from broken to valid and nowhere else, which is what `update` cannot do at all, since it loads before it writes. `broken` is its reading half and asks the same question, so a caller is never shown a file it may not send back.
- [pty.rs](src/pty.rs): `attach`'s command run under a pseudo-terminal, opened by workspace name or, since [ADR-0022](../../docs/adr/0022-a-socket-may-address-a-session-rather-than-a-workspace.md), by machine and session — bytes out, bytes in, resize, and a `Drop` that detaches without ending the session. The third ssh call shape: `Exec` is one-shot with `RequestTTY=no`, `yantra attach` hands the process over with `execve`, and a browser terminal is neither. Shares `ssh.rs`'s connection options through `Ssh::tty_argv`. **Reconnecting is opening another one** — tmux draws the pane for every client that attaches, so no replay buffer belongs here (Y-132, Q5). `run` and `run_on` (Y-394, [ADR-0030](../../docs/adr/0030-a-one-off-terminal-runs-only-a-command-an-install-left.md)) run a command an install left under a terminal of its own with no tmux, as `TERM=… /bin/sh -c '…'`, and `exited` reads the status `ssh` reports once the output ends. [tests/install.rs](tests/install.rs) types a real sudo password into one and the install completes.
- [history.rs](src/history.rs): one pass of the redaction job ([ADR-0032](../../docs/adr/0032-the-appliance-keeps-the-conversation-history-encrypted.md) decision 2, Y-430). It reads the Claude, Codex, Gemini and Grok transcripts under `$HOME` and writes a redacted copy of each under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/yantra/history/<harness>/`, the folder Syncthing sends. `gitleaks stdin` finds the secrets with its own rules and one Yantra rule for `NAME_PASSWORD=value` (R18 §11.3's miss); Rust replaces each with `[REDACTED]`. It fails closed: a file is not staged when gitleaks fails, when a reported secret is not in the text as written, or when a JSON line would stop parsing, and no gitleaks on PATH stops the pass. A copy is rewritten when the live file's mtime moved, and every copy is rewritten when the rules or the gitleaks version change; a copy it cannot rewrite then is removed. A copy goes when its live file goes. The staging directories are 0700, and a directory it cannot read fails only itself. The live transcript is never written. opencode keeps its sessions in SQLite and is out of scope.
- [heartbeat.rs](src/heartbeat.rs): the seven-field wire type `yantra-agent` sends and `yantrad` reads. `deny_unknown_fields` for the same reason as `workspace`, and a two-variant `Power` so unknown power cannot be expressed (ADR-0013).
- [placement.rs](src/placement.rs): `rank`, a pure function from candidates to a ranking (Y-452). A machine ranks when its beat *arrived* within 30 s; `sent_at` is never read. The score is R5's RAM headroom (20), CPU idle (15) and power (10), each rounded to one decimal, plus 30 when the repository is on the machine and R5's session affinity (20) when a workspace there names it (Y-517). The score is the sum of the terms (I-10), and a repository that could not be asked about scores 0 and filters nothing. `reason` turns the terms that fired into a short phrase. `ask` fills the repo and affinity terms for a `Wanted` repository or folder: it asks only the machines with a fresh beat, over ssh through a fakeable `Find`, for at most 5 s each, and matches a workspace by the path's last segment for a repository and the whole path for a folder. `POST /api/placement` and `yantra why --repo` both call it. Ties go to the name. Power is never a filter (ADR-0013 §2), and a rejection carries ADR-0013 §7's reason: never heard from, not reporting, or asleep or off. The shape is T3 Code's `load-balancing.ts`, credited in its block comment ([ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-the-chat-is-a-stream-json-bridge-in-the-daemon.md) decision 5).
- [notify.rs](src/notify.rs): the difference between two consecutive looks at the fleet, and one send (Y-146). `Watch::look` is pure and the whole decision: **the first call returns nothing**, because a daemon that persists nothing has no previous state and must not announce the fleet at every reboot; a machine that could not be asked **keeps** the verdicts it had, because unknown is not changed; a workspace the answering machine no longer lists is dropped. `AwaitingTrust` is the verdict that matters most (I-49) and the only one that is news whatever came before it; everything else is a `Running` that stopped being one — never `NoAgent`, never `Stopped`, and **never a telemetry threshold** (ADR-0013's non-goals). `post` is one attempt over `ureq` on a blocking thread, and a failure is the notification gone. **`Notification` carries a workspace and a verdict and has no field for a machine or a repo**, and `Relay`'s `Debug` is hand-written because the token is a secret (§B4, Q5) and so is the topic in the URL — no error carries either. **The relay is a general publish channel** and the notifier is only its first caller (Y-147, answering Q16): `post` takes a `Message` — a body, and ntfy's `Title` and `Priority` as options — a `Notification` renders into one — its `Title` is the fixed headline of one of six phases copied from T3 Code (Y-451), a failed run's body is the fixed string *The agent run failed.*, and the body is cut at 160 characters, while `Display` keeps the full verdict for the event log — and **the body is the caller's**, so nothing here composes a workspace's resolved secret into what leaves. **`write_relay` and `write_github` are the only things that write the file** ([ADR-0021](../../docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md), [ADR-0023](../../docs/adr/0023-the-github-grant-lives-beside-the-relay.md); Y-199, Y-342): each rewrites its own lines in `RELAY_FILE` — `/etc/yantra/daemon.env`, which the unit reads with `EnvironmentFile=` — and keeps every other line verbatim, so writing the relay never erases the grant, `write_github(None)` is `logout`, and a client id an operator typed survives both. Mode `0600` when it creates the file; it refuses a URL with no scheme and refuses a value holding a quote, a space or a newline rather than escaping it, since either would be syntax to systemd's parser. `test_message` is what the CLI and the dashboard both send, and it names nothing about the fleet. `from_env` builds a `Relay` from `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` and `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN` and from nowhere else; an absent URL is no relay and is not an error.
- [snapshot.rs](src/snapshot.rs): what a caller last learned about the fleet and when — machines, workspaces, sessions, agents, readiness and what is waiting on GitHub. Each class carries its own age; "nobody has looked yet" is `None`, and a look that succeeded can still carry a broken workspace file (Y-141). No clock and no loop — those are the daemon's.
- [snapshot.rs](src/snapshot.rs): what a caller last learned about the fleet and when — machines, workspaces, sessions, agents, readiness, and the caller's own GitHub credential. Each class carries its own age; "nobody has looked yet" is `None`, and a look that succeeded can still carry a broken workspace file (Y-141). No clock and no loop — those are the daemon's.

## Decisions that constrain this crate

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): core logic is a library; binaries stay thin. The source of the never-print rule.
- [ADR-0006](../../docs/adr/0006-ssh-exec-transport.md): why the transport looks over-engineered and is not.
- [ADR-0007](../../docs/adr/0007-workspace-schema-v1.md): the workspace schema, with provisioning as an explicit non-goal.
- [ADR-0009](../../docs/adr/0009-machine-names-are-ssh-destinations.md): a `machine` is an ssh destination; `~/.ssh/config` decides what it means.
- [ADR-0011](../../docs/adr/0011-claude-code-runs-as-a-tui-in-tmux.md): the agent is a TUI in tmux, the transcript is the log, and Yantra sends it no input.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): what a heartbeat carries, why each field earns its place, and why absent power data means AC.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): this crate's invariants — the largest share in the project. The single most useful thing to read before changing anything here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the crate's own working rules, including which invariant binds which module.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): a symlink to CLAUDE.md, for agents that read AGENTS.md.
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): project state — milestones, open tasks, decisions, risks.
- [tests/common/mod.rs](tests/common/mod.rs): the disposable sshd + tmux container every integration test runs against.
- [tests/manual_macbook.rs](tests/manual_macbook.rs): the `#[ignore]`d checks that need the real MacBook rather than a container — `just test-mac <machine>`. Two need a person at that machine and refuse without one: Y-139's measures whether a transcript keeps advancing while the tmux session is detached (Q12, R-1), and Y-151's asks whether the gate finds a credential inside a GUI-login tmux server where ssh finds none (ADR-0018 §5, I-44). Both need that server started from a GUI login, which is the one thing no container can stand in for.
- [tests/pty.rs](tests/pty.rs): Y-127's spike — ssh connections differing only in how the local end is given a terminal, answering whether `^C` reaches a process in a remote pane — followed by Y-128's tests of [pty.rs](src/pty.rs) itself, in the same container, and Y-132's two: a terminal dropped and another opened is drawn the screen the first one left, including a full-screen application on the alternate screen. It is where I-18 was finally measured; its header says what each arm found.
- [tests/ssh_identity.rs](tests/ssh_identity.rs): Y-144 — the identity [identity.rs](src/identity.rs) prepares, reaching a real sshd **by name alone** through the config it wrote, and `ssh.rs`'s known-hosts half proved rather than assumed. Every connection is made from a keypair generated at test time, with `-F` at that config and `IdentityAgent=none`, and each test first asserts the connection is *refused* — it only works once the generated public key is placed, so nothing of the developer's can be what authenticates. What it cannot prove is that OpenSSH finds the file at all: that path comes from `getpwuid`, not `$HOME`.
- [tests/two_clients.rs](tests/two_clients.rs): Y-131 — two live clients on one tmux window, which is what a second browser tab is. Pins I-54 and falsifies R2's *"the smaller clamps pane size"*; `window-size manual` is measured beside it as the rejected alternative.
